title: Case G — flow behind a tree belt

status_meaning.scored: a validation run exists and its scores are in cases/{id}/validation.json
status_meaning.running: the solve is in progress; no scores yet
status_meaning.not comparable: the engine cannot produce the measured quantity at the measured location: OpenLB at the resolution this hardware runs, FluidX3D without a ground wall function; the measurement behind each is on the Validation page

results.quantity: U/U_H and k/U_H^2 at the 28 points, U_H the wind at the tree height (7 m): the measured mean scalar speed against the modelled |U| and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k), both over the model's own U(7 m) at x = -35 m, and over the imposed U_H = 5.299 m/s; LAD and Cd are not in the dataset
results.normalisation: the field's U/U_H and k/U_H^2 (U_H = the wind at the tree height, 7 m, during each period) against the model's |U| and k over the model's own U(7 m) at x = -35 m ('own approach') and, in the second set of scores, over the imposed U_H = 5.299 m/s ('imposed'); the model is also scored as sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k), because the field is the mean of an instantaneous speed; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05
notes: LAD and Cd are not in the dataset (only the shading rate, 81 %). The drag values are crowns of the Eddy3D vegetation library.

The three crowns are entries of the Eddy3D vegetation library (Cd·LAD 0.30, 0.625 and 0.875 1/m, loss coefficients 1.2, 2.5 and 3.5). The arm nearest the 28 values says which library crown the belt resembles.
Eddy3D models trees as a Darcy-Forchheimer momentum sink only: there are no canopy k or epsilon source terms. The modelled k behind the belt follows from the inflow and the shear layer over the belt.

The slab arms idealise the belt as two-dimensional (the belt through both slip planes, infinite width; the data paper's Figure 7 draws a two-dimensional tree); the half-belt arm is the real 74 m belt on a half domain with its centre plane on the symmetry plane. Both are scored against the same 28 values.

The tabulated inlet carries the workbook's inflow over a smooth floor (the site's roughness is not in the model), so the approach flow does not stay the imposed profile: in the open-field arm it is 1.19 of it at 1.5 m and 0.995 at 7 m at x = -10 m, and the model's U(7 m) at x = -35 m is 0.976 to 0.984 of the imposed U_H. The headline scores divide the model by that own U(7 m).
The field is the mean of the instantaneous speed of a 3-D sonic anemometer, which exceeds |U| in a turbulent wake: the model is scored as |U| and as sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k), the bracket of Cases C to E.

The approach profile and the wake were measured on different days (28 and 26 December 2000), and the approach k does not match the workbook's own inflow note (k/U_b^2 = 0.20 at 9 m against the note's constant 3.02 m^2/s^2, 0.096 U_b^2). The files do not explain the mismatch.
Every arm ran to the 3000-iteration limit with the residualControl unmet; the epsilon initial residual at the last iteration was 2.7e-2 to 3.6e-2 in the slab arms and 3.2e-2 in the half belt.

Every arm with trees shows a velocity deficit directly behind the belt against the open field, recovery with distance, a speed-up through the 1.2 m gap, and more drag slowing the lee more and pushing more wind through the gap.

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

figures.caption: Case G, measurement lines and planes: A to G vertical profiles, x/H = 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Positions in multiples of H.

Case G, OpenFOAM 12 (realizable k-ε), the drag sweep: the field's U/U_H and k/U_H² at the 28 points against the modelled |U| and k over the model's own U(7 m), one column per arm: no belt, three crowns of rising Cd·LAD and the real 74 m belt as a half domain. LAD and Cd are not in the dataset. Dots take the colour of the line or plane they were measured on: the letters and colours of the layout figure of the case.

Case G, OpenFOAM 12: the mean U/U_H and the mean k/U_H² over the four heights at each of the seven stations behind the belt (x/H = 0.25 to 5), the field against each arm of the drag sweep. The letters A to G mark the seven lines of the layout figure.
Case G, OpenFOAM 12, conifer crown of the drag sweep: the field's U/U_H against the modelled |U| over the model's own U(7 m) at four of the seven masts behind the belt, offset by 1 per mast.

results.pairs_columns: arm (open-field, pine, conifer, screen or half-belt-conifer: the five runs share this file), point_id (the table's, 1-28), x (m behind the leeward face) and z (m above ground), full scale; U_meas and k_meas, the field's U/U_H and k/U_H^2; U_model and Urms_model, the modelled |U| and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) over the arm's own U(7 m) at x = -35 m (u7_mps, in m/s), k_model, k over u7_mps^2; U_model_imposed and Urms_model_imposed, the same over the imposed U_H = 5.299 m/s

Every arm with trees shows a velocity deficit directly behind the belt against the open field, recovery with distance, a speed-up through the 1.2 m gap, and more drag slowing the lee more and pushing more wind through the gap.

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)
